text: You time a serial run and a parallel run. Speedup is \(S = {{c1::T_{\text{serial} }/T_{\text{parallel} } }}\). Efficiency is \(E = {{c2::S/p }}\). Linear speedup means \(S = {{c3::p }}\).
extra: Ideal linear speedup gives \(E = 1\). Real runs usually land lower.

text: Amdahl with serial fraction \(a\): \(S = {{c1::1/((1-a)/p + a) }}\). As \(p \to \infty\), \(S\) caps at {{c2::\(1/a\)}}.
extra: The serial slice sets the ceiling no matter how many cores you throw at the parallel part. Use that bound when you pick \(p\).

text: Add more processes and efficiency \(E = S/p\) usually {{c1::falls}}, because thread management, mutexes, network I/O, and file I/O all grow with \(p\).
extra: Speedup can still climb while \(E\) slides down. That is the overhead tax.

text: Memory model: Pthreads share one {{c1::address space}} and sync with mutexes. MPI uses {{c2::separate processes}} that pass messages. Warp keeps {{c3::host and device}} memory apart, so you copy data in first.
extra: Kernels then run on device memory. This is the first axis on the study-guide compare table.

text: Where it runs: Pthreads are threads on a {{c1::shared-memory}} machine. MPI is processes across {{c2::one or more nodes}}. Warp pairs a CPU host with an {{c3::NVIDIA GPU}} (or a CPU fallback).
extra: MPI can span machines. Warp is heterogeneous GPGPU.

text: Built-ins: Pthreads give you {{c1::barriers}} and DIY reductions. MPI ships rich {{c2::collectives}} like Bcast and Reduce. Warp fires {{c3::kernel launches}} over \(N\) elements.
extra: No collectives in Pthreads. MPI collectives are the big win for chunky distributed work.

text: Best fit: reach for Pthreads on {{c1::fine-grained}} shared-state updates. Pick MPI for {{c2::large independent chunks}} with modest messaging. Warp wins on {{c3::uniform data-parallel maps}} big enough to pay for copies.
extra: Match the model to communication cost and how fine the work is.

text: Classic traps: Pthreads hit {{c1::data races}}, deadlocks, and oversubscription. MPI hangs on {{c2::mismatched tags}} or ranks, plus tiny chatty messages. Warp dies on {{c3::excessive host-device copies}} or problems too small to amortize transfers.
extra: These are the signature failure modes on the compare table.
